arxiv-2109-00636.title: Neural networks and standard cosmography with newly calibrated high redshift GRB observations
arxiv-2109-00636.creator: and Martin Hendry
arxiv-2109-00636.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by and Martin Hendry. Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) detected at high redshift can be used to trace the cosmic expansion history. However, the calibration of their luminosity distances is not an easy task in comparison to Type Ia Supernovae (SNeIa). To calibrate these data, correlations between their luminosity and other observed properties of GRBs need to be identified, and we must consider the validity of our assumptions about these correlations over their entire observed redshift range.

arxiv-2202-02894.title: Effects of Parametric and Non-Parametric Methods on High Dimensional Sparse Matrix Representations
arxiv-2202-02894.creator: Sayali Tambe, Raunak Joshi, Abhishek Gupta, Nandan Kanvinde, Dr. Vidya Chitre
arxiv-2202-02894.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sayali Tambe, Raunak Joshi, Abhishek Gupta, Nandan Kanvinde, Dr. Vidya Chitre. The semantics are derived from textual data that provide representations for Machine Learning algorithms. These representations are interpretable form of high dimensional sparse matrix that are given as an input to the machine learning algorithms. Since learning methods are broadly classified as parametric and non-parametric learning methods, in this paper we provide the effects of these type of algorithms on the high dimensional sparse matrix representations.

arxiv-2503-23475.title: Many-body quantum chaos and time reversal symmetry
arxiv-2503-23475.creator: Weijun Wu, Saumya Shivam, Amos Chan
arxiv-2503-23475.description: Abstract We investigate universal signatures of quantum chaos in the presence of time reversal symmetry (TRS) in generic many-body quantum chaotic systems (gMBQCs). We study three classes of minimal models of gMBQCs with TRS, realized through random quantum circuits with (i) local TRS, (ii) global TRS, and (iii) TRS combined with discrete time translation symmetry.

arxiv-2510-06074.title: On algebro-geometric quotients of torus-invariant subvarieties of the flag variety
arxiv-2510-06074.creator: Luis Yair Meza Pérez, Pedro L. del Ángel R, Carlos Pompeyo-Gutiérrez, Miguel Angel Dela-Rosa
arxiv-2510-06074.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Luis Yair Meza Pérez, Pedro L. del Ángel R, Carlos Pompeyo-Gutiérrez, Miguel Angel Dela-Rosa. In this paper, we study the subvarieties of a complex flag variety that are invariant under the action of a maximal torus. Using combinatorial techniques derived from matroid theory, we introduce a decomposition of this variety into affine, locally closed subsets, which we refer to as thin Schubert cells , each indexed by an element of a Cartesian product of matroids.

arxiv-2512-08900.title: Deterministic randomness extraction for semi-device-independent quantum random number generation
arxiv-2512-08900.creator: Pablo Tikas Pueyo, Tomás Fernández Martos, Gabriel Senno
arxiv-2512-08900.description: Abstract It is a well-known fact in classical information theory that no deterministic procedure can extract close-to-ideal randomness from an arbitrary entropy source. On the other hand, if additional knowledge about the source is available—e.g., that it is a sequence of independent Bernoulli trials—then deterministic extractors do exist.

pmc-10693036.title: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease associated with greater herpes zoster risk than alcoholic fatty liver disease
pmc-10693036.creator: Cheng-Wei Yu, Chia-Hung Chen, Yung-Chi Cheng, Wen-Che Hsieh, Tzu-Ju Hsu, Fuu-Jen Tsai, Chao-Yu Hsu
pmc-10693036.description: BackgroundDisease-related stress can trigger the occurrence of herpes zoster (HZ). Fatty liver disease (FLD) can have adverse effects on the human body and may induce stress in affected individuals. In this study, we investigated whether FLD is associated with an elevated risk of HZ.

pmc-10737284.title: THE ACHIEVE RANDOMIZED TRIAL: EFFECT OF HEARING LOSS INTERVENTION ON COGNITIVE DECLINE IN OLDER ADULTS
pmc-10737284.creator: Jennifer Deal
pmc-10737284.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Hearing loss in older adults is linked to accelerated cognitive decline and incident dementia in population-based observational studies; whether intervention can reduce cognitive decline is unknown. The multi-center NIH-funded ACHIEVE randomized controlled trial is testing efficacy of a best-practices hearing intervention (amplification and rehabilitation) versus a successful aging health education control intervention, on 3-year cognitive decline in 977 dementia-free adults aged 70-84 years with untreated mild-to-moderate hearing loss.

pmc-11583095.title: Solid-Phase Reactivity-Directed Extraction (SPREx): An Alternative Approach for Simultaneous Extraction, Identification, and Prioritization of Toxic Electrophiles Produced in Water Treatment Applications
pmc-11583095.creator: Daisy
pmc-11583095.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Current strategies to assess water quality are ineffective at prioritizing the most toxic chemicals within a treated water sample. Although it is well known that oxidation byproducts (OBPs) from water treatment processes (e.g., chlorination and ozonation) are linked to adverse health outcomes such as skin diseases, reproductive toxicity, and various cancers, we are still unable to account for a large fraction of the toxicity drivers.

pmc-11664707.title: Clinical Results of Os Subfibulare Resection with Ligament Repair in Chronic Lateral Ankle Instability
pmc-11664707.creator: Jae Wan Suh, Youngchae Park, Joohan Kwon, Hyun-Woo Park
pmc-11664707.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Category:Sports; AnkleIntroduction/Purpose:Previous studies still have conflicting views on the size of the ossicle during ligament repair after ossicle removal. However, there is no standard for measuring the size of the ossicle. Furthermore, ossicle has various sizes, shapes, and positions.

pmc-11676847.title: The Effect of Muscle Cramps During Hemodialysis on Quality of Life and Habitual Physical Activity
pmc-11676847.creator: Gabriela Kot, Agata Wróbel, Kasper Kuna, Agnieszka Makówka, Michał Nowicki, Francis Dumler, Ronald Castelino
pmc-11676847.description: Background and Objectives: This study aimed to evaluate the association between QoL, self-assessed physical activity, and the presence and severity of muscle spasms in chronic hemodialysis patients. Patients undergoing regular in-center hemodialysis (HD) have much lower quality of life (QoL) than healthy individuals.

pmc-12385179.title: Oculometric Assessment of Sensorimotor Impairment Associated with Liver Disease Is as Sensitive as Standard of Care Cognitive Tests
pmc-12385179.creator: Dorion Liston, Katherine Wong, Aaron Yeoh, Shalonda Haywood, Aparna Goel, Paul Kwo, Quinn Kennedy, Philip N Okafor, Ruth Marchand Tappen, Mónica Rosselli
pmc-12385179.description: Significance: Hepatic encephalopathy (HE) occurs in 20–80% of patients with liver cirrhosis, impacting attention, memory, processing speed, and visuospatial skills. HE standard-of-care psychometric assessments are time-consuming and require staff training. Oculometrics may provide a fast, non-invasive brain health assessment that can be self-administered in a medical environment.

pmc-12628436.title: Enhanced Visualisation of Colorectal Tumours via Topical Application of EMI-137 in a Methylcellulose-Based Formulation: An ex vivo Feasibility Study
pmc-12628436.creator: Elham Zonoobi, Daan G. J. Linders, Stefan Harmsen, María Rita Rodríguez Luna, Shadhvi S. Bhairosingh, Dima D. A. Almandawi, Ronald L. P. Van Vlierberghe, Marvin W. J. Nogaitzig, Christophe Portal, Stijn A. L. P. Crobach, Michele Diana, Gilbert Noordam, Davey van den Burg, Elke E. M. Peters, Andreas
pmc-12628436.description: BackgroundFluorescence-guided molecular imaging may improve colorectal cancer (CRC) patient outcomes by enabling early detection and better surgical treatment, relying on developing targeted fluorescent tracers to highlight tumours. This study investigates visualising primary colon tumours by topically applying EMI-137, a targeted fluorescent tracer designed to bind to c-Met receptor.

pmc-12805729.title: The NOD (Naltrexone for Overdose Prevention) study protocol: a pilot randomized controlled trial of intramuscular naltrexone for opioid overdose prevention among people who use stimulants living with or at risk for HIV
pmc-12805729.creator: Ayesha Appa, Xochitl Luna Marti, Stefan Baral, Steven Shoptaw, Alexander R. Bazazi, Matthew A. Spinelli, Dave Glidden, Monica Gandhi, Phillip Coffin
pmc-12805729.description: BackgroundDrug-related mortality in the United States continues to transform, marked by a surge in overdose deaths involving both fentanyl and stimulants. This pattern presents specific risks for people at risk for and living with HIV, who have high rates of stimulant use and disproportionate risk of opioid overdose due to unintentional fentanyl use.

pmc-13185716.title: An Interdisciplinary Young Adult Pain Rehabilitation Program
pmc-13185716.creator: Leah Reece, Morgan Mitcheson, Carolina Donado, Julie Shulman, Monique Ribeiro, Kevin Zirko, Roxanne DeFabio, Shealyn O’Donnell, Paige Brousseau, Lisa Volpigno, Mahadeva Daniel, Sophia Paravalos, Kimberly Lobo, Mikayla Culpo, Deirdre Logan, Navil Sethna, Christine Greco
pmc-13185716.description: Context:Chronic pain affects 1 in 9 young adults worldwide. Intensive interdisciplinary pain treatment (IIPT) has shown favorable outcomes in improving in pain intensity, mood, school attendance, and social and physical functioning in pediatric studies. However, few IIPT programs are designed for young adults (YAs), a distinctly vulnerable developmental stage.

pmc-13264019.title: Genetic heterogeneity alleviates behavioral trade-off between exploration and vigilance in Drosophila
pmc-13264019.creator: Takahira Okuyama, Daiki X Sato, Yuma Takahashi
pmc-13264019.description: SummaryBehavioral trade-offs are a major constraint on animal performance, but group living can reshape such constraints. Using genetically distinct strains of Drosophila melanogaster, we examined how aggregation and heterogeneity shape the exploration-vigilance trade-off under predator-like looming stimuli. A latent negative relationship between exploration and vigilance became apparent when aggregated, suggesting improved behavioral performance compared to solitary condition.

pmc-13273969.title: Community perspectives on canine-mediated rabies risk in the Klang Valley, Malaysia: implications for outbreak preparedness
pmc-13273969.creator: Yunusa Adamu Wada, Mazlina Mazlan, Mohamed Mustapha Noordin, Mohd Azmi Mohd-Lila, Siti Zubaidah Ramanoon, Nurul Izzati Uda Zahli, Lau Seng Fong, Nur Ahdanisa Khairul Muzammil
pmc-13273969.description: BackgroundDespite being declared rabies-free in 2012, Malaysia has experienced a resurgence of canine-mediated rabies since 2015, with the Klang Valley, a densely populated urban hub, facing an increasing threat. The success of elimination efforts hinges on community engagement. Yet, baseline data on public knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) in this critical region are limited.
